HENRY WINTER: Jordan Pickford has seen off five England challengers but hasn't faced a threat quite like James Trafford

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (949 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fourfourtwo

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Since succeeding Joe Hart as England’s No.
  • But Pickford’s age, 32, and the quality of his main challenger now, 24-year-old James Trafford, means he knows he’s now in the biggest fight of his England career to remain No 1.
  • This is not to call time on Pickford’s England career.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since succeeding Joe Hart as England’s No. 1 in the 2017/18 season, Jordan Pickford has seen off significant challenges from Aaron Ramsdale, Nick Pope and Dean Henderson with other keepers like Jack Butland, Fraser Forster, Sam Johnstone, Tom Heaton and Jason Steele also involved in squads.

He’s used to competition. But Pickford’s age, 32, and the quality of his main challenger now, 24-year-old James Trafford, means he knows he’s now in the biggest fight of his England career to remain No 1.

This is not to call time on Pickford’s England career. It’s actually more to celebrate that England have two exceptional goalkeepers who have huge respect for each other and will push each other.

According to recent reports, pickford still has a role to play. It was only back in March that we were lauding Pickford for keeping a clean sheet for 923 minutes, comfortably an England record. He then conceded only eight goals in seven World Cup games - and was unbeaten in the two Florida warm-ups. Writing Pickford off is premature.

What Sunday night’s epic events in Madrid confirmed is that Trafford is Pickford’s obvious successor and the changeover may be quicker than anticipated.

Sources indicate that trafford is probably now favourite to start for England at Euro 2028. Such headlines will drive Pickford on even more. The Wearsider is very proud, very patriotic, is understandably determined to reach a century of caps (he’s six shy) and he’s always felt slightly under-appreciated.

In a recent development, pickford deserves more respect. He’s played in the semi-final of two World Cups and in the final of two European Championships. Pickford helped England overcome their fear of shootouts.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

He saved five penalties in shootouts at four different tournaments and even took one – and scored. Such service to his country cannot be dismissed lightly.

I’ve watched Pickford closely in training, hearing the impact as he throws his body around, leaping up, often slapping his gloves together in approval at a save or simple self-encouragement.

According to recent reports, his language is very lively at times. During one session filmed by the media at Euro 2024, Pickford was heard half-laughing, half-concerned that one failed save attempt would end up all over the internet.

Sources indicate that pickford is far more emotional and vocal than Trafford, partly rallying his defence but also charging himself up. He needs that adrenaline charge. Get the rave on, to quote one of his sayings.

Recent findings suggest that trafford, who grew up on a farm in Cumbria, helping his dad herd sheep, is more sanguine, more controlled, and that may appeal more to Thomas Tuchel. He’s less hyper than Pickford. He also offers more of what Tuchel wants in distribution. Growing up at Manchester City, Trafford was coached to pass out from the back. Pickford launches his booming deliveries downfield but not always accurately. Trafford is more precise, picking out his wingers well. He can be vulnerable to the quick press, though. Trafford’s still developing.

But if Trafford’s time has truly come with England, he will reflect on successfully negotiating difficult times. Re-signing for Man City after a successful two seasons at Burnley should have been a re-start, embedded as No. 1, but then Gianluigi Donnarumma arrived, and Trafford was benched. Moving to Leeds United proved inspired.

Sources indicate that it’s impossible to say that Trafford came of age in Madrid as he has to deliver week after week, minimising mistakes and improving decision-making. He’s 24, playing regularly, and will mature even more into a fine goalkeeper with great shot-stopping strengths and sound distribution.

Industry observers note that trafford certainly impressed against Spain, making reflex saves from Fermin Lopez and then the follow-up from Aymeric Laporte. It is these double saves where Trafford most impresses. Late on, protecting the 3-2 lead, Trafford watched like a hawk as Lamine Yamal glided in from the right. A keeper has to make so many decisions in such short, intense passages of play, perhaps lasting only a few seconds but demanding total concentration and swift reactions, mental and physical.

In a recent development, yamal could have whipped an early shot to the near-post, so Trafford had to guard that. He then stepped across as Yamal, using Anthony Gordon and Myles Lewis-Skelly to try and mask his intentions, targeted the far-post. Trafford was equal to the threat, dropping smartly to his right, pushing Yamal’s curling strike away. He remained alive to the continued threat. Marc Cucurella now had the ball.

Recent findings suggest that all those drills in training, the reflex save and then jumping up for the follow-up developed the muscle memory for Trafford. Cucurella’s driven return was complicated further by a slight deviation off Ben White. Trafford readjusted in a split-second and pushed the ball around the post. Trafford truly saved the day.

Recent findings suggest that england’s No. 1 shirt is up for grabs now. The Nations League quarter-final in March will clarify who is the owner. If Trafford keeps delivering for Leeds, the smart money is now on him to retain it. One thing can be stated for certain: England have two very good goalkeepers.

Washington Spirit clinch third consecutive trip to NWSL Championship with win over Utah Royals

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1055 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After two runner-up finishes at the NWSL Championship, the Washington Spirit will get a third consecutive shot at lifting the big prize.
  • The Washington Spirit rallied from an early deficit to defeat the Utah Royals 2-1 in front of another sold-out Audi Field.
  • It has been revealed that the Royals arrived in D.C.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After two runner-up finishes at the NWSL Championship, the Washington Spirit will get a third consecutive shot at lifting the big prize.

The Washington Spirit rallied from an early deficit to defeat the Utah Royals 2-1 in front of another sold-out Audi Field. The Spirit weathered the fastest goal in NWSL playoff history, then flipped the script within minutes and never took their foot off the pedal or lost control. Utah Royals' Cloe Lacasse struck first on the scoreboard, and Sofia Cantore and Clara Luvanga provided the decisive goals for the Spirit, while Trinity Rodman brought plenty of spark and Andi Sullivan supplied reliable, steady play in the midfield.

Here's how the Spirit rallied for the win:.

It has been revealed that the Royals arrived in D.C. early in the week, avoiding a nationwide flight stoppage on Friday, and fresh off a huge quarterfinal upset -- a 1-0 win against the No. 2 seed San Diego Wave FC. They wasted little time to show their early playoff win was no fluke.

In the opening two minutes, Utah won a corner kick, and Lacasse created multiple moments of history. Her service into the box curled toward the near post, creating some miscommunication between goalkeeper Sandy MacIver and her defenders, and the ball snuck into the net. It was the fastest goal scored in NWSL playoff history and the first-ever olimpico scored in the postseason.

CLOÉ LACASSE OLIMPICO IN THE SECOND MINUTE 😱@UtahRoyalsFC off to a FLYING start the @NWSL semifinal!Watch the action LIVE on @CBS and @paramountplus! pic.twitter.com/UfWxDcSB5Y.

The early breakthrough stunned the typically rowdy crowd, though the set-piece tally was hardly a surprise, considering Utah's ability this year. The squad scored 15 goals off set pieces this season, with seven headed goals, so Lacasse's ability to score from the flag was just one more highlight for its set-piece playbook.

The early lead should have been a boost for the visiting side, but instead, it opened up the game; the Spirit then tested the Royals with relentless attacking pressure.

According to recent reports, the Spirit needed just six minutes to turn things around. Washington's attacking trio combined for the equalizer, with Luvanga finding Rodman out wide in space, and the winger swiftly connecting with Cantore in front of goal.

Sources indicate that SOFIA CANTORE WITH THE BACKHEEL 🤯Her seventh goal of 2026 is her first playoff goal to bring @WashSpirit level 1-1!Watch the action LIVE on @CBS and @paramountplus! pic.twitter.com/C8J63tVzQn.

"I think getting scored on in the first few minutes will really humble you, and a little bit of a wake-up call, but I thought our response was incredible right after and all game long," Sullivan stated after the game.

"As soon as we responded after the goal, I think even when we got scored on, I had full confidence that we would get it done," she noted.

In a recent development, sullivan's role in controlling the game as the Spirit closed out the first half was notable. She's the longest-tenured player on the active Spirit roster right now, with goalkeeper Aubrey Kingsbury out on maternity leave. Sullivan herself returned to the squad after an ACL injury and then maternity leave. The defensive midfielder completed all of her tackles (three) and aerial challenges (four) and captained the team on the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that "She represents a lot of the values that we want to have as a team, as a club, on and off the field, and right now she's reaching that peak of performance. I'm very, very happy and proud of her because it's been tough for her. Obviously, coming from a long injury, and then maternity leave. So being able to come back to get fit again and try to compete at this level; it's not easy, and she's a role model. An example as a captain with the young players, new players, and being able to do a lot of things," Spirit head coach Adrian Gonzalez said after the game.

In a recent development, "Whatever the team needs, she's kind of that voice. Very happy and proud of her because I know what this means to her and also for us. Having her again and being able to play a final is huge for her and for us," he said.

Recent findings suggest that while Utah managed to stave off attacking sequences by the Spirit to close out the opening half, the Spirit's game-winning goal came in the early minutes of the second half. A poor back pass by Utah in their own half was the final dagger. Luvanga pounced on the mistimed pass, and a smart touch inside the box beat goalkeeper Mandy McGlynn.

CLARA LUVANGA POUNCED ON THIS PASS 😮‍💨Her second goal in her second playoff match and the @WashSpirit are one step closer to returning to the @NWSL Final!Watch the semifinal LIVE on @CBS and @paramountplus! pic.twitter.com/f0uUfUU19K.

The Tanzanian international has only been on the roster since September, but her impact on games has grown week to week, and now she can add a game-winning NWSL playoff goal to her resume.

Recent findings suggest that "It's not the first one that she scores like that. Obviously, she puts a lot of pressure on centerbacks, keepers, and that is very contagious. When you see that your forward is pushing and jumping and pressing like that. Everyone who is behind they follow her, and also creates a lot of doubts and nerves on the opponent team, not facilitating the build-up. And obviously, that was, I think, a massive shot of energy," Gonzalez said after the game.

"I think it was also a little bit of release, knowing that 'okay, we did the most difficult thing' that was coming back after we conceded a goal, and yeah, happy again because she's bringing a lot. Both attacking and defending, and obviously she's learning so quick and having a huge impact.".

In a recent development, what's next The Spirit will face the winner of Sunday's semifinal between Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current. This will be the Spirit's third consecutive appearance in the NWSL Championship. When the league revealed a neutral site for the 2026 NWSL Championship, it selected Audi Field, and now the Spirit have a chance to play in a home playoff final on Nov. 21.

Victims of Nazi war in Poland call on Germany for support

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1039 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "We can no longer wait," declared Polish victims' organizations in a dramatic appeal to German civil society, published on November 5 on the website of the Foundation for Polish–German Reconciliation.
  • "Around 50,000 survivors of Nazi persecution during the German occupation still live in Poland today.
  • According to recent reports, the open letter pointed out that many of the survivors are over 90 years old, struggling with illness and rising costs, and in need of help in their daily lives.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"We can no longer wait," declared Polish victims' organizations in a dramatic appeal to German civil society, published on November 5 on the website of the Foundation for Polish–German Reconciliation.

"Around 50,000 survivors of Nazi persecution during the German occupation still live in Poland today. They include former concentration camp and prison inmates, people deported to Germany for forced labor and those subjected to other forms of Nazi repression," wrote the signatories of the appeal.

According to recent reports, the open letter pointed out that many of the survivors are over 90 years old, struggling with illness and rising costs, and in need of help in their daily lives. "For many, any further delay in deciding to provide assistance means that help will come too late," noted the appeal, which was distributed in German, Polish and English.

While Germany has recognized its moral responsibility toward the remaining survivors of Nazi persecution, the signatories pointed out that a corresponding decision on possible reparations by the German federal government has yet to be made.

"Today, we appeal primarily to German civil society to provide humanitarian support to survivors of Nazi persecution living in Poland," they wrote, addressing businesses, foundations, associations and private citizens. "Every donation matters.".

The unresolved problem of war reparations has clouded German-Polish relations for decades.

Following the 1989 democratic transition in Central and Eastern Europe and the reunification of Germany, the federal government provided 500 million deutschmarks to Holocaust victims in Poland. More than 1 million people received support through these funds. Former forced laborers also received payments from the EVZ Foundation, which works to preserve the memory of the victims of National Socialist persecution.

However, given the scale of German crimes during World War II, the reparations provided to date have been considered as insufficient by large parts of Polish society. German occupation policy in Poland was characterized by systematic crimes against the Polish population. An estimated 6 million Polish citizens were killed during the war, including about 3 million Polish Jews.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sources indicate that as part of the "General Strategy East," a large portion of the population was to be displaced, enslaved or murdered. As early as 1939, the "Intelligenzaktion" specifically targeted the Polish elites, including teachers, clergy, civil servants and intellectuals. In addition, approximately 2.5 million Poles were deported to the German Reich for forced labor and made to work there under inhumane conditions.

Sources indicate that when it came to power in 2015, Poland's right-wing conservative Law and Justice Party (PiS)  made the glitch of war reparations a central focus of Warsaw's policy toward Berlin. The PiS government estimated Poland's war losses at 6.2 trillion zloty (approx. €1.3 trillion/$1.58 trillion) and officially demanded this sum from Berlin in October 2022.

According to recent reports, the center-left government led by Donald Tusk has distanced itself from these demands since Tusk's election victory in December 2023. However, the government has also made no secret of the fact that Poland is expecting a "creative solution" from its German partner, according to Foreign Minister Radek Sikorski.

Former German Chancellor Olaf Scholz had offered €200 million ($224 million) prior to his visit to Poland in the summer of 2024, an offer rejected by Tusk as insufficient. The talks held since then between Berlin and Warsaw have failed to produce a solution.

In a final declaration following the German-Polish government consultations in December 2025, the German government promised to "analyze possibilities for additional support for Polish victims of Nazi aggression and the German occupation of Poland.".

"Currently, there is no decision regarding a humanitarian gesture and the draft budget reflects this status," Josef Hinterseher, deputy spokesperson for Germany's Federal Foreign Office, told reporters on September 23.

Germany's opposition Greens party has not given up hope of a turnaround in its efforts to secure a "humanitarian gesture.".

"Our parliamentary group submitted a request to the budget committee to secure funding for this 'humanitarian gesture.' Unfortunately, the request was rejected," Franziska Brantner, co-chair of the Greens, told DW on Thursday in Warsaw.

Recent findings suggest that "Hope dies last, so we will do everything in our power to ensure that the coalition makes this change after all," she emphasized. Brantner sees the budget committee's "final review session," which will take place this week, as a last chance.

The matter of reparations still plays an key role in Polish society, even more than 80 years after the end of the war. There is hardly a family that did not suffer during the war. In the latest German-Polish Barometer — a representative survey that has been conducted for 25 years — 53% of respondents stated that the suffering of the Polish people is not sufficiently acknowledged in Germany. Only 18% believed that the Germans have done enough.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has been revealed that jakub Deka, chairman of the Foundation for Polish–German Reconciliation, believes the appeal by the victims' associations could now mobilize Germany's civil society. Following an initial appeal in May directed at the German federal government, several hundred Germans responded with donations ranging from €50 to several hundred euros.

According to recent reports, to date, a total of more than €35,000 ($39,000) has been deposited into the foundation's account. Several people in need have already received one-time assistance from this fund. "It's a drop in the bucket, but every little bit helps," Deka told DW.

Sources indicate that the foundation's chairman quotes Jerzy Tarasiewicz — who led the victims' association in the Polish city of Gdansk for many years — as a cautionary reminder. In January, Tarasiewicz was quoted in an interview with the daily newspaper Gazeta Wyborcza as saying: "They [the Germans] are waiting for us to die.".

Tarasiewicz, who was born in 1942 on a German farm where his parents were performing forced labor, died in late September at the age of 84 without being able to witness this "humanitarian gesture.".

"It is a painful reminder that the victims cannot wait any longer," said Deka.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tottenham Hotspur are to move for a new striker, as their search for goals intensifies.

The Lilywhites endured a terrible start to the season under manager Robert De Zerbi and were the last team in the Premier League to pick up a win – but after encouraging signs in recent weeks, it appears that they may have turned a corner.

With Tottenham struggling to score goals, however, a new forward has been earmarked for the January transfer window.

Spurs were mentioned to be interested in Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi over the summer, but with the recent France international picking up a foot injury in preseason, any move to a bigger was put on hold.

De Zerbi instead brought in Omar Marmoush from Manchester City, with the Egyptian job-sharing the No.9 role with Dominic Solanke – though the pair have just two league goals between them this term.

With the North Londoners lacking a reliable hold-up man who can also offer threat in behind, attention has turned to Igor Matanovic of Freiburg.

Speaking on the Market Madness podcast, transfer expert Ben Jacobs claimed that the Croatian is an option for a loan move in January that Spurs could explore, with Bournemouth closing the door on Kroupi leaving midseason.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

The Cherries sold Semenyo to Manchester City in January – though the Ghanaian international only left when his release clause was triggered – and the south coast outfit are determined not to see another talent leave in the same way this campaign.

“If [Spurs] can’t find the right target, or maybe someone with a bit more experience within the Premier League, then they can reassess in the summer,” Jacobs claimed.

“What they won’t want to do is necessarily go all in and panic buy in January for someone on a long-term contract, instead of just biding their time and waiting it out.”.

Tottenham spent around £400 million in the summer building a side that finished 17th two years running, smashing their transfer record twice and recruiting seven newly introduced faces.

Every one of De Zerbi's signings over the summer – including youngsters such as Cole Ramsey and backup goalkeeper Martin Dubravka – was signed from an English side.

Matanovic is worth €30m, according to Transfermarkt. Tottenham take on Ipswich Town when Premier League action resumes after the international break.

#1244. Super subs, xG kings and $150 million question marks: The Premier League's most intriguing players

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2288 w)
📖 Baca
Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

Super subs, xG kings and $150 million question marks: The Premier League's most intriguing players

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2288 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that whatever you might think about the November international break, there is one fact you simply will not be bothered to argue against: it is well timed for the statistically-minded football fan in your life.
  • Industry observers note that we are not yet, then, at the stage where we can always draw hard and fast conclusions.
  • According to recent reports, spend $100 million on a player who turns 29 next week and the expectation is surely that a player will hit the ground running.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that whatever you might think about the November international break, there is one fact you simply will not be bothered to argue against: it is well timed for the statistically-minded football fan in your life. A 10-game sample size -- that's the useful stuff. At this point, many but not all teams are what their analytics tell us they are. It's similar but not quite the same for players. Not many have hit the 900-minute mark yet, but plenty are at 500-plus, a body of evidence that usually isn't warped by any one good or bad game. Of course, it depends on how good or bad that game is.

Industry observers note that we are not yet, then, at the stage where we can always draw hard and fast conclusions. We are, however, in a position to find some interesting questions. Here are five of them, in player form:.

According to recent reports, spend $100 million on a player who turns 29 next week and the expectation is surely that a player will hit the ground running. That's especially true when they're Bruno Guimaraes, terror of Premier League midfields in a Newcastle United shirt, a player who had long since seemed ready to step up to a Champions League contender. While it would be fair to say that the Brazilian's form is nothing like a problem for table-topping Arsenal, he has not exactly started like a house on fire. Mikel Arteta has acknowledged as much whenever he has spoken about Guimaraes, even when served up the opportunity to praise him after what seemed an impressive performance against Hull City.

"He's hitting serious levels now, but we can still take him to another level. That's my conviction; I told him that in the dressing room -- he owned a lot of moments in the game, but there is still much more to come." It would be fair to say that, Hull aside, the best levels he has hit have been as a substitute. When he comes off the bench, he passes more accurately, wins more tackles, creates chances and scores brilliant goals. As a starter, he has occasionally looked a beat off his teammates.

Physical data from Gradient Sports hints as to what the issue might be. For every 90 Premier League minutes on the field, Guimaraes covers less of it at sprint speed (≥25 km/h) than any outfield player bar Mikel Merino and spends notably more time jogging than anyone, an average of 30 minutes. Compare Guimaraes to Declan Rice, an admittedly vertiginous bar, and it is easy to see why the fresh guy looks off the pace.

In a recent development, equally, it explains why he's such a compelling substitute. When the other 21 players on the pitch are flagging, Guimaraes' comparative physical challenges go unexposed and he can run the show.

That's all well and good for now, but he can't carry on like this, can he? You would have to assume that Myles Lewis-Skelly will have to make way even if the academy graduate's emergence as a midfield option unlocked an improved Declan Rice at the tail end of last season. The second most expensive signing in your history can't be an impact guy off the bench behind the homegrown kid, right? Probably not, but if there's any team that could justify the idea of Guimaraes as a 12th man, maybe it's Arsenal, where they pride themselves on their game-changing finishers.

Recent findings suggest that erling Haaland's Swiftian reign at the top of the Premier League xG chart has been interrupted, at least temporarily, by an unlikely source. You'd have to go back to the days of a marauding Romelu Lukaku for the last time an Everton striker looked like they might rule the roost. Only once since the Belgian's departure has an Evertonian cleared 20 goals in all competitions. In the last five, even a dozen has been beyond this club.

It has been revealed that thierno Barry isn't there yet, but boy is he on the right trajectory. His 7.28 non-penalty expected goals (npxG) puts him 0.22 ahead of Haaland and nearly 2.5 npxG up on anyone else in the league. Expand the pool to Europe's top five leagues and he is breathing rarefied air behind the top four of Lamine Yamal, Donyell Malen, Raphinha and Kylian Mbappe, all of whom have the advantage that they are not playing for an upper midtable outfit in the continent's most competitive division. And in that environment, Barry is making the hardest thing in the sport look easy: getting good shots in prime locations.

If Barry were turning them in as often as he was getting them, Everton might be even higher than sixth. Still, six goals through 10 games is not to be sniffed at, particularly when the pressure on the 24-year-old was so intense. The bungling of a deadline-day move for Folarin Balogun, as Beto moved to Fiorentina, meant it was Barry or bust for David Moyes this season.

Sources indicate that perhaps it was an enforced show of faith for a player who was in and out of the XI last season, his first in England, that brought the best out of the former Villarreal man. His manager views the success in more straightforward terms. "He has settled down a bit more," said Moyes after Barry's brace helped down Coventry. "His language, his understanding, his communication is much better and he has worked hard to get himself in those positions to score.".

It is easy to see why getting the soft factors right might have been all that was required. Barry is the ideal striker for the modern Premier League. Tall, strong and mobile -- he ranks third among center forwards for top speed this season, per Gradient Sports -- he can serve as an outball when a press needs beating and then get in the box. He might not have the technical elegance of an Mbappe, but he makes his presence felt and occupies high-value spaces. That is more valuable than it sounds, as proven when James Tarkowski's howitzer from range deflected in off him. You might not like it, but this is what elite center forward play looks like. Long may it continue, at least as far as Everton are concerned.

Sources indicate that there are three types of underrated footballers. First, your common-or-garden-variety underrated footballers, often to be found plying their trade at Wolverhampton Wanderers or Burnley. Ashley Westwood, in that season, put up stupidly high xA numbers. Then there are the so-often-dubbed-underrated that they actually become a bit overrated. Leighton Baines. Lee Carsley. They don't have to play for Everton, but it does help. Olivier Giroud is another. See, not all Everton.

Recent findings suggest that the most rarely spotted of the underrated is the chameleonic one, correctly pegged for a while, only to develop to the point that he is underrated in a completely different way to how he once was. Take Alex Iwobi. Some time ago, a consensus coalesced around the Nigeria international that he was a good player for a team at Fulham's level (and indeed Everton's). Any minute he was on the field, he would probably be delivering good performances for good Premier League teams.

Industry observers note that not anymore. Ten games in and Iwobi looks like one of the outstanding creative forces in the Premier League, critical to the march towards adequacy that Fulham have undertaken after a slow start to life with Alvaro Arbeloa.

Among true playmakers, Iwobi is one of the best at getting the ball into dangerous areas and creating for his teammates. Iwobi leads the league in expected assists with 2.95 and is tied with Bruno Fernandes for most passes completed into the penalty area. Only Pascal Gross has created more chances.

Sources indicate that those players can't match Iwobi when it comes to ball progression either. In terms of advancing the ball not just into the box but from deeper, Fulham's ball-playing fulcrum on the inside left channel has completed more progressive passes than anyone not named Declan Rice or Jan Paul van Hecke.

Sources indicate that when Iwobi broke through at Arsenal, he displayed a preternatural sense for how to keep attacks alive, the pass before the pass before the pass. Now a 30-year-old, Iwobi still does that more than he unpicks defenses. One cannot argue, however, that he is not putting his teammates in the right spot. It is just that not everyone quite appreciates how often he does so just yet, including his own supporters, who jeered Iwobi when he was substituted in the early-season defeat to Crystal Palace. Since then, he has responded to his critics in style, teeing up two or more shots in each of Fulham's last seven Premier League matches. If a few more of them had been converted, in fact, if any of them had been converted, then Iwobi might not still be underrated.

Sources indicate that the upper reaches of the list of most expensive transfers of all time are hardly all bangers all the time, but of the biggest money moves in the sport's history there are only a handful where at such an early stage you find yourself wondering if anyone really understood what the plan was. Manchester City committed the best part of $150 million on Enzo Fernandez this summer, a fee only eclipsed by Neymar and Kylian Mbappe. Beyond a vague sense that it would be nice to give new manager Enzo Maresca one of his favorite players, what was it they had in mind?

Sources indicate that we pointed out earlier in the season that the aggressive positioning of Fernandez in the 5-3 win over Sunderland looked extreme; at the time it seemed reasonable to view it as a reflection of a stretched-out, chaotic game. Maresca had, of course, unlocked more number 10-ish qualities in the Argentine at Chelsea, but surely that had been reflective of what that team needed, particularly as Cole Palmer went off the boil? Perhaps not. Fernandez keeps popping up in the sort of positions that leave Elliot Anderson on an island. It is one thing to view Anderson as the fresh Rodri, quite another to immediately throw the England international in at the deep end, tying a whole midfield together by force of will.

Of course you could sketch out a logic for why you might push Fernandez high. It is not so long ago that City deployed two playmakers in front of a sitting midfielder and they ruled the Premier League. Fernandez and Rayan Cherki aren't Kevin De Bruyne and David Silva though.

Maybe Cherki could be offering a level of creation on a par with City greats; he started well enough last season. In year two, he is creating lower-quality chances, his expected assists per 90 dropping by 50%, notably more than the slight uptick in the quality and quantity of shots he is taking. It's no surprise that Cherki is creating less when fewer of his touches are coming in the attacking third. The output has been there so far, five goals and two assists in nine Premier League games, but for that to continue, Maresca might want to be getting his No. 10 into more dangerous spots.

Instead, those seem to be going to Fernandez, who has not proven himself able to get the final-third production to justify his platforming. For every 100 touches he takes, he is delivering significantly less npxG+xA than in either of the previous two seasons. Meanwhile, he is less effective without the ball than he has been at any stage since coming to England. That's no wonder. If an opponent passes through City's frontline, then Fernandez does not have the mobility to get back.

Industry observers note that as such, to enable themselves to get perhaps a shot or two more than they would get with Ayyoub Bouaddi or Mateo Kovacic next to Anderson, City have made themselves an even more vulnerable side to the counterattack, already giving up more fast-break openings than they did in 2020-21 or 2021-22. Carry on like this, and Fernandez will become one of those nine-figure transfers, the ones that live in infamy.

It was a signing that delighted a city when it was unveiled in early August, and rightly so. Loaning Carl Rushworth from Brighton had been an inspired bit of business by Coventry City, the then-24-year-old goalkeeper anchoring the best defense in the division as Frank Lampard's side returned to the top flight for the first time in over a quarter of a century. A club-record £22 million fee seemed a snip for such a young talent.

All of that is worth bearing in mind given the struggles Rushworth has endured this season: saving just 53.7% of shots he has faced, conceding 5.19 more goals than the xG value of the shots he has faced. The swagger of last season has been replaced by a sloppiness apparent in both the goals he conceded in the second half against Tottenham, weak gloves doing nothing to repel efforts that came at him a bit quicker and a bit sooner than they might have last year.

None of this needs to be a problem for Rushworth. In 2023-24, James Trafford was another highly touted young goalkeeper afforded a shot at the massive time by Burnley. He was obliterated up and down the Premier League, his first touch in the division picking the ball out of the net off Erling Haaland. Those struggles were the making of him, as they have broken others. It'll be some time yet before we discover which way these past few months send Rushworth.

Latest Update: Band-Edge-Extended Heterointerfaces for Perovskite Solar Cells and Tandems

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (748 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have emerged as a promising photovoltaic technology, with efficiencies rapidly approaching those of established crystalline-silicon solar cells.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have emerged as a promising photovoltaic technology, with efficiencies rapidly approaching those of established crystalline-silicon solar cells. Further efficiency gains, however, are increasingly limited by charge extraction and recombination at the interface between the perovskite absorber and the electron-transport layer. Interfacial modifiers are widely used to suppress these losses, yet many conventional ammonium-based modifiers are weakly electronically coupled to the perovskite surface and can introduce barriers to electron extraction 1-5. Here we realize electronically coupled heterointerfaces by introducing a family of heteroatom-containing, fully conjugated formamidinium interfacial modulators, establishing band-edge-extending conjugated heterointerfaces that overcome the bottleneck of inefficient interfacial electron transfer. The resulting band-edge-extended heterointerface establishes delocalized electron connectivity at the perovskite/electron transporting layer (ETL) interface and suppresses interfacial non-radiative recombination. We report a certified power-conversion efficiency (PCE) of 27.96% and a stabilized power output (SPO) of 27.84% for inverted PSCs. The corresponding devices retained over 95% of their initial efficiency after 2000 h continuous maximum-power-point tracking under 1-sun irradiation (ISOS-L). Extending this strategy to monolithic perovskite–silicon tandems enables a certified SPO of 34.71%, establishing band-edge extension as a broadly applicable approach to overcoming the conventional trade-off between interfacial passivation and charge extraction.

Manchester City surely cannot win the Champions League with a defence leaking goals and a goalkeeper making errors. But when Erling Haaland is in the team, anything seems possible.

This thrilling victory for City perfectly sums up their season: needless goals conceded, Gianluigi Donnarumma making a mistake, followed by Haaland saving the day with a winning goal.

“How can you stop Haaland?” read the headline in the local Volkszeitung newspaper on the morning of this Champions League clash. The answer is that it has been impossible for RB Leipzig.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League group stage match between RB Leipzig and Manchester City from Saxony. The hosts started the day in 27th place in the 36-team table after two defeats, both by four goals to one, in away games against Como and Real Madrid. City begin proceedings in 12th after victories over Porto and AEK sandwiching that rip-roaring 4-2 defeat by the champions PSG at the Etihad.

City, who seemed in rude health after seven successive wins at the start of the Premier League campaign despite the guilty verdicts in the Premier League’s case against them for financial cheating, have wobbled since then, losing their last two league games. Marc Guéhi and Gigi Donnarumma are both suffering bouts of poor form, other individual errors continue to plague them and, although they are creating hatfuls of chances, they have been thwarted by a combination of imprecise finishing and the excellence of Zion Suzuki and Bart Verbruggen.

In a recent development, for all their travails on the road – RB Leipzig have also lost at Werder Bremen, Bayer Leverkusen and Bayern Munich – they have won all their home Bundesliga matches as well as a 1-0 victory over PSV in this competition. Their total of 22 league goals is second only to Bayern’s 27 and Antonio Nusa, a Norway team-mate of Erling Haaland, is in sparkling form flitting behind strikers Christopher Nkunku and Romulo. City, whose full-backs, if you can describe the centre-backs and midfielders who play either side of the centre-halves in that way, never look fit for purpose defensively and may well have their work cut out tonight if he drifts wide.

Sources indicate that the Red Bull coaching principles, which have treated us to the dross football of Jesse Marsch, Matthias Jaissle and Ralph Hasenhüttl, all about the long pass, the central channel, counter-pressing and second balls, have a upcoming proponent in Martín Demichelis, the forner City and Argentina defender who won the title in 2014 at the Etihad. Three years ago he led River Plate to the title in Argentina, the highlight of a coaching career also spent running Bayern’s U21s, Monterey and Mallorca.

These two have met six times in the last five years, City winning four, most notably the 7-0 thrashing at the Etihad in 2023’s Round of 16, the year they went on to win the Treble. Leipzig’s only victory came at home five years ago in the sixth, redundant group game when City and PSG had already clinched qualification for the knockout stages.

Antoine Semenyo is City’s only absentee; Leipzig will have to do without one-cap Germany midfielder Assan Ouédraogo and former Chelsea striker Marc Guiu.

Kansas City Current's grit earns them spot in NWSL Championship while Gotham's logistics problems linger

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2237 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • LATEST YORK – The awkward logistics of Sunday's NWSL semifinal at Icahn Stadium, a quirky little venue sandwiched on an island in between Manhattan and Queens, were supposed to give way once Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current took to the pitch for one of the league's showpiece matches.
  • "I've been working on free kicks all year," Bethune mentioned post-match, the Current justified in their decision to sign her last winter even if the validation was no longer needed, "and a lot more leading into the playoffs so just practice makes perfect.".
  • According to recent reports, icahn Stadium's irregularities, though, seemed to reflect the game it unexpectedly became the host of six days earlier.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

LATEST YORK – The awkward logistics of Sunday's NWSL semifinal at Icahn Stadium, a quirky little venue sandwiched on an island in between Manhattan and Queens, were supposed to give way once Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current took to the pitch for one of the league's showpiece matches. When the Current's Croix Bethune opened the scoring in the 20th minute with an incredible looping shot off a free kick, the theme of the day was in motion. The league would make the best of the unideal circumstances with a top-quality soccer game, or at least with a few highlight-reel moments nestled into a match contested by a collection of the world's most talented players.

"I've been working on free kicks all year," Bethune mentioned post-match, the Current justified in their decision to sign her last winter even if the validation was no longer needed, "and a lot more leading into the playoffs so just practice makes perfect.".

According to recent reports, icahn Stadium's irregularities, though, seemed to reflect the game it unexpectedly became the host of six days earlier. The Current's 2-1 win came courtesy of a chippy game strategy that would have been the case if the match had taken place at a traditional soccer-specific stadium but it felt especially at home at Icahn Stadium and amidst its elements. The teams played against the wind during Fresh York's first properly cold weekend of the season, and Gotham faced a setting sun that impacted their vision during the first half. Bethune's impressive strike was really the only on-field spectacle to be witnessed on Randall's Island.

BEND IT LIKE BETHUNE 💫 KC takes the lead!NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/F4mQePT5QJ.

"We knew it was going to be a physical game, without a doubt," Current forward Haley Hopkins stated. "Like I said a million times, Gotham's a very, very good team and so we had to be super disciplined in our structure and catch them on their transition and we were just able to put the ball in the back of the net when we had our opportunities.".

According to recent reports, the introduction of Gotham's Rose Lavelle, who has been dealing with niggling fitness challenges over the last few weeks, did not change the smash-and-grab energy of the game. Much as there was a week ago in their quarterfinal win over the Seattle Reign, there was a dull quality to Gotham's attack despite their star power. Over 180 minutes of possession play, the NWSL Shield winners managed zero shots on target and 0.66 expected goals, their midseason marquee signing Sam Kerr managing no shots along the way and mustering just one attempt in her last five matches. To say they were unlucky would be a stretch but their lively start to the second half gave their failed attempts to put a shot on frame a comedic feel.

"I think we were kind of our own worst enemy today," midfielder Savannah McCaskill noted. "I think at times we played into what they wanted to do and their style of play. They want a very chippy game. They want to get into tackles. They want to draw fouls. They want to break up the game. They want to play long and that's not our style. We want to keep the ball. We want to control tempo, and we like to play pretty football. That's [what] we pride ourselves on … but I think we need to find a better way to balance that out, especially in this league. How can we meet the demand of a chippy game while also controlling the tempo? I think we did a really good job when we played them at home the last time [a 2-1 win on Aug. 14]. They scored early but then we completely dominated the rest of the game and I think we failed to do that today and so I think that's really the determining factor.".

In other words, it was the perfect setup for Gotham to equalize off an own goal from Laney Rouse, a week after benefiting from another own goal from the Reign's Jordyn Bugg. Those two goals would be the only ones in their postseason run, just as one might expect from the NWSL Shield winners and reigning champions who entered the playoffs as the favorites to win another title.

Gotham FC find a way to tie up the semifinal 💪NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/Itbzs4Bhz1.

According to recent reports, gotham goalkeeper Ann-Katrin Berger then slipped into game-saving mode with two important blocks while defender Tierna Davidson did what she could to hold the Current at bay, attempting to create a villain arc rivaled only by Argentina's run to the World Cup final. Though the hosts had lucked their way into an even game by the 88th minute, the dark and cold conditions at a downsized stadium in an obscure part of Upcoming York meant the game beckoned for extra time. One final smash and grab was undoubtedly in the cards, though where it would come from was hard to guess – the Current had put in the work to win but soccer's chaotic nature had already weaseled its way into the game.

In the end, it was the Current's Haley Hopkins who had the final say in the 89th minute off of – what else – a set piece, a free kick that led the forward to finally evade Berger with a shot off the crossbar. After losing to them twice in three previous meetings this season, the Current earned their spot in next week's NWSL Championship (Saturday, 8 p.m. ET, CBS, Paramount+) on the back of a well-executed gameplan.

HALEY HOPKINS CLUTCH OFF THE CROSSBAR 🤯The KC Current lead 2-1!NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/BT2OZhwX1y.

It has been revealed that "As much as we tried to analyze certain teams in the league that have given them trouble, we really took information from the games we've played against them, all the ways they challenged us," Current head coach Chris Armas said. "There's been games even where they get high [expected goals], too much progression, too much in our box and we just tried to then look at all the scenes and moments when we made it hard for them so we just tried to take from yesterday and apply it to today, [that] type of thing. We gave up zero shots on goal in 90 minutes. The commitment from our players to just will themselves to it to stick to a match proposal that was going to be largely about taking away spaces, controlling the middle of the pitch and if we can do that on the day – and and we did that by running after them, too, and pressing in moments of high intensity – we not only might stop what they're trying to do on one end and maybe force the turnovers that could challenge them so a little bit of a chess match there in moments.".

Industry observers note that the Current were no slouches, finishing fourth in the regular season and now on a  seven-game winning streak en route to next week's championship. Bethune's star quality shone on Sunday, while the team's record with two-time NWSL MVP Temwa Chawinga and U.S. women's national team standout Michelle Cooper is formidable. It did not erase the fact that they slayed a giant along the way, knocking out the Shield winners and a team that had picked up five major titles in four seasons.

"Gotham has just raised the bar around the league and in our country here, so the way they play, the way the coach sets them up, the talent on the team, the type of games they can put you in, you have to come with a proposal," Armas stated. "They're a team that, again, if iron sharpens iron type of thing, we try to push teams and we try to raise the bar.".

Gotham, though, had not looked the part of the NWSL's gold standard team. Their drastic run, while right now headlined by USWNT players Lavelle and Jaedyn Shaw, is built on the back of an effective defensive structure that has carried an inconsistent offense. Lavelle and, in particular, Shaw have picked up much of the slack en route to the NWSL Shield and Kerr was supposed to bolster their attack after Esther Gonzalez's shock departure for Saudi club Al Qadsiah. They finished the regular season sixth in the NWSL for expected goals with 49.01 but had a genuine finishing problem, notching just 39 goals and ranking in the league's bottom six in that category. Head coach Juan Carlos Amoros is not sounding the alarm just yet but as they enter another offseason, the attacking composition of the team deserves yet another look.

"Of course, we want to create more chances, more shots," Amoros remarked. "We all do but we look at the way we play. We look at the way we create chances. We look at who does that. I think when it comes to these games, could we have [made] some better decisions? Yes, we did. We actually create some good moments. Yes, I wouldn't over-think about it. Something that I'm happy [about]? No but at the same time, we work a lot to make sure that those moments happen. So you know the set pieces, those situations, the open plays, final decisions … Definitely, something that we want to be better [at]. We want to score more goals. I think that we are the best team defending in the league with our aggressive approach to defending but we want to also be able to create and score more goals.".

More importantly, though, Gotham were not treated like the bar-raising team they have become over the years. Icahn Stadium has its charms and is a worthy inclusion on the list of wacky and wonderful places that embody American soccer, an enjoyably chaotic slice of the world's most popular game. It was also a back-up proposal for a team that has called Sports Illustrated Stadium home for five years, settling in nicely to a state-of-the-art soccer-specific build for MLS' Red Bull New York that can hold 20,000 more fans than the 5,000-seater Icahn Stadium can. The pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium, managed by RBNY, had fallen into disrepair and with the primary tenants' end-of-season friendly scheduled for the night before, there was not enough time to fix it. The quirks of Icahn Stadium only served as a reminder that Gotham – and the NWSL – should not have actually been there, even if the field at Randall's Island was better suited for the occasion.

"I want to be really clear and direct in saying that in these types of situations, the field is never an excuse," winger Midge Purce noted. "We lost today because we weren't the better team. That being said, I would say it's inexcusable. It's not what you want in a professional league. It's not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it's a bad look for everyone involved and we always want to be at Sports Illustrated [Stadium] in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season but I would say it had no effect on performance today.".

According to recent reports, the Current's trip to Icahn Stadium is not where the NWSL's efforts to make lemonade end, either. Saturday's semifinal, in which the Washington Spirit beat the Utah Royals to book their spot in a championship game at their home of Audi Field, only added to it. One of the Spirit's sponsors underwrote the costs to push the start time of the Secretaries' Cup, a Division III football game, by a few hours but both matches were played on a field with soccer and football lines. The football lines will likely be faint but visible for next week's NWSL Championship, while the playability of the actual field will probably face a few questions in the build-up.

Industry observers note that "I think we will never know what happened if we would have played [at Sports Illustrated Stadium] on a good pitch," Amoros noted. "I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable under our view. The last couple of games we picked up injuries. Luckily, nothing that has been a season-ending injury but we have to protect our players and guarantee the quality of football so to thank the club, obviously.

"Overall, I think it's been a sad weekend. I think also the situation in Washington yesterday. This league deserves better. The two, arguably, best teams, [most] consistent, having to deal with these situations and then yesterday, you sit down to watch that game around the world and you're seeing those American football lines across today. Credit to the club and the fans. I think they've done an amazing job here. The fans welcomed us. The club has really shifted everything to play here but we couldn't play in our ground where we could have had more people, where we are unbeaten in 13 games at the moment and but I think we took that decision, putting players' safety first, and the outcome is the outcome.".

UK Privy Council overrules Trinidad and Tobago gay sex law

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A man from Trinidad and Tobago has won a legal appeal lasting almost a decade in the last court of appeal available to him — the judicial committee of the Privy Council in former colonial power Britain.
  • Jason Jones, a gay man born in Trinidad and Tobago, had challenged the Caribbean nation's Sexual Offences Act outlawing consensusal sex between adult males, saying that it breached his fundamental rights under the country's constitution.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A man from Trinidad and Tobago has won a legal appeal lasting almost a decade in the last court of appeal available to him — the judicial committee of the Privy Council in former colonial power Britain.

Jason Jones, a gay man born in Trinidad and Tobago, had challenged the Caribbean nation's Sexual Offences Act outlawing consensusal sex between adult males, saying that it breached his fundamental rights under the country's constitution.

He initially won his case at Trinidad and Tobago's High Court, but the government and religious organizations managed to partially overturn the ruling once more, prompting Jones to the take the case to the island nation's highest appellate authority — the Privy Council in  the UK.

"To discriminate against somebody simply because of who they choose to love is simply ridiculous," Jones told the Associated Press after Tuesday's judgment was rendered.

The Privy Council in London is the final court of appeal for some Commonwealth countries including Trinidad and Tobago, although that concern was already contentious in some circles prior to Tuesday's ruling.

A panel of five judges unanimously allowed Jones' appeal, dismissing a counter-appeal from the Caribbean country's Attorney General.

It found that two sections of the country's Sexual Offenses Act 1986, criminalizing "buggery" and "serious indecency" respectively among same-sex couples, violated Jones' fundamental rights to private and family life set out in the 1976 constitution.

The court wrote in its ruling that "the rights and interests of Mr Jones which are at stake involve a particularly important facet of his existence and identity since the ability to form an intimate and loving relationship with another person lies at the core of the right to private and family life.".

The anti-gay laws that call for up to five years in prison have not been enforced in recent history, but critics say they still send an intimidating message.

Judge Philip Sales said as he unveiled the ruling that "the current understanding of the fundamental individual right to respect for private and family life is that it protects such a core part of human identity as one's sexual orientation.".

Sales added that "laws which seek to criminalize such activities cannot be justified.".

Trinidadian authorities argued that because the 1986 laws were passed with a super-majority and constituted criminal penalties that dated back to colonial times, prior to the constitution, they could be considered "existing law" and override the individual constitutional rights in certain circumstances.

But the Privy Council judges found that the so-called "proviso" for this special status — "unless the Act is shown not to be reasonably justifiable in a society that has proper respect for the rights and freedoms of the individual" — had not been met.

One of Jones' lawyers, Anand Ramlogan, is a former attorney general of Trinidad and Tobago and argued against this position earlier in the case.

According to recent reports, "Constitutional rights exist precisely because majorities are not always right," Ramlogan noted. "They ensure that the dignity and equality of every citizen are not left to the changing tides of public opinion.".

Jason Jones is a 61-year-old born in Trinidad and Tobago.

Openly gay since the age of 16, he noted he fled the country in 1996 because of homophobic violence and discrimination.

Speaking to the Associated Press on Tuesday after what he termed a "stunning victory," he noted he would describe himself as a "very angry gay man," whose anger had helped him persist in his legal appeal for so many years.

"Society has treated me worse than a criminal," he said. "There is a real sense of vindication with this judgment. Finally, the courts are seeing that they need to step up because our politicians are so toothless.".

He said he became inspired to speak out after losing friends to HIV/AIDS and after meeting American singer-songwriter Nina Simone when she toured the island nation for three weeks in 1984, when he was 19.

"Nina was the one who said, 'Jason, get off this rock and go see the world,'" he said, calling it a defining and life-changing experience.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Trinidad and Tobago's government, the country's Council of Evangelical Churches and its largest Hindu organization, Sanatan Dharm Maha Sabha, contested the case, which has wound its way through several courts since the appeal was launched in 2017.

According to recent reports, in 2018, Trinidad's High Court found the laws unconstitutional. But in 2025, a local appeals court partially reversed the ruling. Trinidad's Court of Appeals subsequently allowed Jones to seek a ruling from the final appeals court in England.

The case was being closely watched by activists across the Caribbean, with similar laws in place in several other countries in the region.

The Bahamas decriminalized homosexuality in 1991.

The UK repealed laws in overseas territories Anguilla, the British Virgin Islands, the Cayman Islands, Montserrat and the Turks and Caicos Islands in 2001.

In a recent development, judges in Barbados, Dominica, St. Lucia and Antigua and Barbuda have also recently struck down similar laws.

But in former British colonies Grenada, Jamaica, Trinidad and Tobago and St. Vincent and the Grenadines it remains a crime.

It has been revealed that the UK only decriminalized gay sex in 1967, more than four centuries after the so-called "buggery" laws were first introduced under King Henry VII, and more than a century after the last executions for the crime. People still faced prosecution or the threat of it for consensual adult gay sex until after World War II, with surely the most famous later-years case being that of computing and codebreaking pioneer and war hero Alan Turing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool are accused of having an unbalanced squad this season, however, the club will reportedly resist the urge to recruit a fresh centre-back during the January transfer window.

The Athletic claim that adding to the heart of the defence is 'not a priority' for the Reds, ruling out investment in the position for both the upcoming winter market and the summer of 2027.

Instead of turning to the transfer market to silence critics, the Liverpool hierarchy is placing its trust in the crop of emerging defensive talent to eventually succeed 35-year-old Virgil van Dijk.

Liverpool's decision is largely down to the impact Jeremy Jacquet has had since arriving at Anfield. Behind him, Anfield still has high hopes for a trio of highly-rated youngsters: Giovanni Leoni, who is nearing a return to fitness following an ACL injury last year, Ifeanyi Ndukwe, who is currently on loan with Levante in Spain, and teenage prospect Mor Talla Ndiaye.

Opposition supporters and media pundits have spent much of the season pointing out a lopsided squad that is forcing Iraola into tactical compromises on a weekly basis, as well as Van Dijk's advancing years.

The primary target of this criticism is the club’s full-back situation with Conor Bradley sidelined and Jeremie Frimpong unfancied in a traditional back-four system.

Iraola has been forced to deploy centre-backs, most notably Ronald Araujo, as makeshift right-backs. And while the Uruguayan has brought physical solidity and aggression, asking a traditional central defender to provide the overlapping width hasn't always had the desired effect and on occasion left Liverpool looking somewhat asymmetrical in possession.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Square pegs in round holes is never a sustainable fix, and coupled with a lack of midfield depth, squad planning is never far from the Anfield conversation.

If Liverpool are officially ruling out central defensive reinforcements, even with Virgil van Dijk entering the twilight of his career, funds and focus can theoretically be redirected toward the squad’s weaknesses.

In FourFourTwo's opinion, their January priority must be identifying a specialist right-back and a dominant midfield presence, although Trey Nyoni's emergence as a water-carrier of sorts makes up for that to an extent. The lasting message from the corridors of power at Anfield is that in the centre of defence, Liverpool consider themselves already locked down for the foreseeable future.

Gareth Bale is involved in an investment project to buy Sevilla.

The former Tottenham Hotspur and Real Madrid man retired from playing football three years ago after a stint in Major League Soccer with Los Angeles Galaxy, at the age of 34.

Since retiring, Bale has been occasionally involved in punditry and competed in the February 2023 edition of the AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am golf tournament in California – but now, he appears to be heading down the same route as the likes of Ronaldo and Gerard Pique in owning a Spanish club.

Seven-time Europa League winners Sevilla have fallen on hard times since winning the competition for the last time in 2023, failing to finish in the top half of La Liga for the past four seasons and narrowly scraping relegation in 2025, while city rivals Real Betis go from strength to strength.

Bale played against the Andalusian outfit nine times in his career, registering nine goals and assists – and after leaving Madrid with a fractured relationship between him and fans, he might be about to create more distance by investing at the Estadio Ramon Sanchez Pizjuan.

El Confidecial in Spain are reporting that the Welsh wing wizard is linked to an ownership group looking to take over the club.

American investment fund Juggernaut Capital Partners are one of three groups noted to be interested in the club, along with rival group HD Ventures, led by Saudi brothers Mansour Sayed and Haidar Sayed, who have already held talks with club officials over a possible takeover.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Bale is remarked to be involved purely in an advisory role for now, but with WalesOnline claiming that the former forward is worth £150 million, he could well be involved financially in time – especially considering previous comments.

After being linked with a move to buy Cardiff City, the Wales legend stated that investing in the game was “about being patient, finding the right club, and the right path for us to take,” adding that he was motivated to buy the Bluebirds because of his hometown connection to the club.

Over the summer, Bale's former team-mate Sergio Ramos reached an agreement with an investment group to take over Sevilla – an outfit that he spent two spells with – with a consortium looking to acquire a controlling stake and take on the debt of the club.

This deal fell through towards the end of May, however, with reports of terms shifting mid-negotiation and Ramos denying any bad faith.

Sevilla didn't spend a single penny improving their squad during the 2025 transfer window, making free signings and collecting fees for the likes of Dodi Lukebakio and Loic Bade, before making a net profit again this summer, with their biggest buy, Scottish striker Robbie Ure, for around £5m.

After finishing 13th last term, the Rojiblancos are presently 13th in the table and hosting a Seville derby this weekend.
